Cette approche transversale s’applique à: I work across watchmaking, jewellery, leather goods, accessories, furniture, packaging and visual identity. My role spans positioning and initial research, design refinement and renderings, and working with workshops through development.
Cette expérience illustre une difficulté: This experience illustrates a real difficulty of the profession: a creation does not become freely exploitable because it has been ordered, shown or handed over. The search time, the design and the value of the sign must be recognized, remunerated and framed. Defending this principle also means defending the work of all designers in the face of the appropriation of their ideas.
Cette planche explore des lignes de chau: This board explores shoe lines, their proportions and the relationship between the stem, heel and sole. The sketch allows you to quickly compare several attitudes before specifying a direction.
Cette planche rassemble quinze recherche: This board brings together fifteen logo searches developed around the owl, its look and the movement of its wings. The tracks explore several levels of stylization, from linear drawing to more constructed monogram, in order to identify an elegant, memorizable sign and perfectly suited to the universe of hairdressing, the signboard and printed supports.
Cette planche réunit les premières inten: This board brings together the first intentions. The line remains free and spontaneous: it serves to multiply the hypotheses, to eliminate certain leads and to make emerge a coherent direction.
Cette recherche personnelle imagine une: This personal research imagines a family of fun charms for bags and keyrings. These small colorful characters bring movement, humor and a pop touch to bags that are sometimes very classic or lacking real personality.
Cette recherche personnelle mêle silhoue: This personal research combines fashion silhouettes, bags and accessories. The board links the different elements of a collection and explores how they can share a formal direction.
Cette recherche réunit une famille de mo: This research brings together a family of furniture designed to accompany the uses of a monumental place. Sittings, sofas and outdoor furniture interact with the architecture of the Grand Palais with sober lines, generous volumes and a mastered graphic presence. From the collection drawing to the situations, the project builds a coherent, comfortable and adaptable ensemble to the various spaces and events.
Cette sélection réunit des études et des: This selection brings together studies and projects of different natures. It shows how an idea is built up gradually, from the first gesture drawn up to the definition of a volume, use or collection.
Cette sélection suit l’ordre de présenta: This selection follows the order of presentation of the historical portfolio of Atelier WR. Each visual documents the context of creation, the construction of the model and its formal language.
Cette étude personnelle explore des volu: This personal study explores leather goods volumes and decorations. The proposals compare several bag silhouettes and how a graphic signature can fit into the product.
Chaque charm est pensé comme un accessoi: Each charm is thought of as an accessory in its own right: an expressive object that can be hung, moved or collected. Volumes, fringes and colour assemblies transform leather falls from leather goods into desirable and singular products.
Chaque collaboration peut prendre une fo: Each collaboration can take a different form: one-off mission, global accompaniment, artistic direction or regular exchange on the development of a brand.
Chaque collection part d’un récit visuel: Each collection starts from a clean visual narrative, then declines this language into silhouettes, effects of light, materials and complementary typologies. Saturn explores the orbital imaginary. Aura reinterprets the Space Age. Canopée translates the protective forms of living into an organic light presence. LUMA revisits the traditional lantern through the smoked glass and an immersive light. Heritage transposes the monumental elegance of Art Deco chandeliers into a connected table lamp. Celestine dresses the light of the pleats of haute couture and an option of jewellery pads.
Chaque création recherche l’équilibre en: Each creation seeks the balance between singularity, simplicity and ability to deploy. The sign must remain legible at all scales, cross the supports and maintain its consistency over time.
Chaque dossier part des codes de la mais: Each file starts from the codes of the house and uses to build a coherent creative direction. The research translates into silhouettes, clasps, details, materials, colors and families of products immediately recognizable.
Chaque projet cherche un équilibre entre: Each project seeks a balance between aesthetic presence, comfort, feasibility and experience of use, from the initial concept to the definition of a coherent and identifiable proposal.
Chaque projet commence par une histoire: Every project begins with a story worth telling. I look at its context, heritage, uses, craft and the brand’s ambitions. That story guides decisions about form, materials, detail, packaging, imagery and how the product is presented. It gives the product a clear and lasting identity.
Chaque proposition explore un principe f: Each proposal explores a different formal principle—faceted, circled or curved—while seeking the same economy of means. Cuts, handles and closing systems extend the geometry of the volume in order to create coherent, functional and immediately identifiable bags, in accordance with aesthetics and brand values.

The opening becomes a ritual in several times — unlocking, revealing, sharing — while the research explores several architectures, from double-flying writing to rotating cage, to transform the discovery of the bottle into a true ceremony.

The cosmetic world is inspired by a veil of softness: milky gradients and colorful transparencys evoke the fine texture of the mask and the care placed on the skin. Each formula is associated with a color to identify its ingredients and its benefits while preserving the consistency of the range. At the opening, the pouches connected at one point unfold as a fan: the box becomes a display, facilitates the choice of care and installs a delicate, functional and memorable discovery ritual.

The amulet takes the form of a small rechargeable pochon, filled with odorous traditional herbs. Hand embroidered according to the tradition of Suzhou embroidery, one of the major heritage know-how of this city recognized by UNESCO for its art crafts, the dragon composes his body with ears of wheat, a French symbol of happiness and prosperity. The object combines protection, perfume and ritual in a room conceived as a lasting link between the two cultures.
